text: @agenticcontrolplane/dsh 为 DSH 提供工具调用策略检查。插件挂接 Cordis 的执行前后钩子：调用前将工具信息送至网关并处理允许、审批或拒绝决定；调用后可提交输出供扫描、拦截、改写或产生 shadow 提示。它还汇总会话治理回执，并按交互或后台层级处理网关故障。适合需要集中控制智能体工具权限的 DSH 用户。需要 ACP 凭据，可由 ACP_BEARER_TOKEN 或 ~/.acp/credentials 提供。

@agenticcontrolplane/dsh adds policy checks to DSH tool execution. It asks a gateway to allow, approve, or deny calls, then can scan, block, or rewrite outputs. Session receipts and tier-based outage handling are included. Requires an ACP credential from ACP_BEARER_TOKEN or ~/.acp/credentials.
想让 DSH 在执行 shell 或其他工具前先检查策略。
能不能把需要人工确认的工具调用交给 DSH 审批？
我希望根据策略拒绝智能体执行某些工具操作。
想在工具运行后把输出交给服务检查并拦截不合规结果。
如何把策略网关改写后的工具输出返回给模型？
我想知道每个会话里有多少工具调用受到了治理。
Can I require a policy decision before DSH runs an agent tool?
I need tool outputs scanned and optionally blocked or rewritten after execution.
@agenticcontrolplane/dsh 的功能「执行前策略决策」：工具运行前向 ACP 网关发送工具名、参数和会话信息，并按 allow、ask 或 deny 继续执行、请求审批或拒绝调用。
@agenticcontrolplane/dsh 的功能「执行后输出检查」：工具完成后提交文本结果供 ACP 扫描，服务可以阻断结果、返回改写文本，或提供 shadow 提示。
@agenticcontrolplane/dsh 的功能「会话策略回执」：会话结束时汇总受管工具调用、拒绝、审批和提示数量，并输出当前会话的控制台查看链接。
@agenticcontrolplane/dsh 的功能「按会话层级处理网关故障」：策略服务不可达时，交互会话记录故障并继续调用，后台层级则返回拒绝，避免在无法查询策略时继续工具操作。
@agenticcontrolplane/dsh 会将工具名称、输入参数、会话信息及工具输出发送到配置的策略网关进行检查；凭据通过环境变量或本机 ACP 凭据文件提供。
@agenticcontrolplane/dsh 在无凭据时不执行远端策略检查，工具调用照常运行并记录未治理提示；使用前应配置 ACP 凭据。

[Agentic Control Plane](https://agenticcontrolplane.com) for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness): every tool call is checked against your policies before it runs, and every decision is recorded — what ran, what was blocked, and why.

@agenticcontrolplane/dsh README · @agenticcontrolplane/dsh：> **Which ACP?** dsh also ships `packages/acp` in core — that one is [Zed's Agent Client Protocol](https://agentclientprotocol.com), the editor↔agent standard, published as [`@deepseek-ai/dsh-acp`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deepseek-ai/dsh-acp). Unrelated project, same acronym. If you're wiring dsh into Zed or the AI SDK, you want that one; this plugin decides whether each tool call *runs*. The full map: [agenticcontrolplane.com/acp-vs-acp](https://agenticcontrolplane.com/acp-vs-acp).

@agenticcontrolplane/dsh README · @agenticcontrolplane/dsh：Every decision also lands in your [console](https://cloud.agenticcontrolplane.com) with tool, input preview, decision, reason, latency, and cost — dsh's own Trajectory log and your ACP activity log become two independent witnesses to one history. One workspace covers every harness you run: the same rules answer for dsh, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenClaw. Free for individuals.

This is a native Cordis plugin on dsh's typed interception points, not a shell-hook shim. It registers on:

@agenticcontrolplane/dsh README · @agenticcontrolplane/dsh：- `tools/pre-execute` — the policy decision. `allow` lets the call through, `deny` blocks it with the reason in the trajectory, `ask` hands off to dsh's own approval flow.
- `tools/post-execute` — output scanning. A server-side block turns the result into corrective feedback; shadow-mode notices surface what enforcement *would* have done.

@agenticcontrolplane/dsh README · Install：> dsh itself requires **Node 22** (`Promise.withResolvers`, zstd streams). Under Node 20 the harness fails at boot with errors that don't say so — `fnm install 22` first.

```sh
curl -sf https://agenticcontrolplane.com/install.sh | bash
```

That detects dsh, installs this plugin into every profile you have, opens your
browser once to sign in, and saves the key to `~/.acp/credentials` — which the
plugin reads on its own. There is no token to copy and nothing to export.

@agenticcontrolplane/dsh README · Install：<details>
<summary>Manual install</summary>

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <your-profile> add @agenticcontrolplane/dsh
dsh --profile <your-profile>
```

Credentials come from `~/.acp/credentials` (written by the installer above) or
from `ACP_BEARER_TOKEN` if you would rather set it yourself — useful on a
headless box. Get a key at
[cloud.agenticcontrolplane.com](https://cloud.agenticcontrolplane.com).

@agenticcontrolplane/dsh README · Install：Confirm the row actually mounted — installing the package and composing it into
the profile are two different things:

```sh
dsh --profile <your-profile> --dump-config | grep @agenticcontrolplane/dsh
```

If it isn't there, add `@agenticcontrolplane/dsh` to that profile's `package.json`
`"dsh.profile.bundles"` list.

</details>

No build step, no dependencies, plain ESM. Installing from git works too (`dsh plugin add github:agentic-control-plane/dsh-acp-plugin`) and needs no build allowance.
@agenticcontrolplane/dsh README · Install：No key? The plugin says so loudly and stays out of the way — it never bricks a session.

@agenticcontrolplane/dsh README · Configuration：Override the row in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: acp
  name: @agenticcontrolplane/dsh
  config:
    governBase: https://govern.agenticcontrolplane.com  # or your self-hosted gateway

`ACP_GOVERN_BASE`, `ACP_BEARER_TOKEN`, `ACP_AGENT_TIER`, and `ACP_SHADOW=off` work as environment variables too.

@agenticcontrolplane/dsh README · Failure posture：An outage of the control plane must not brick the harness, and a lapse in coverage must never be silent:

- **Interactive sessions fail open, loudly.** Gateway unreachable → the call proceeds, a `[ACP] ⚠ UNGOVERNED` warning is logged, and a line lands in `~/.acp/lapse.log`.
- **Unattended agents fail closed.** With nobody watching, the block is the safety net.
- Policy denies are unaffected — this posture only covers the inability to *ask* the policy.
@agenticcontrolplane/dsh README · Failure posture：In headless compositions with no approval service mounted, dsh itself resolves `ask` to deny — unattended runs cannot self-approve.
